name: Albugnano

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Dolcetto, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Dolcetto sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Nebbiolo is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
